subject: App stability cheat-sheet: SDK migration, endpoints, and retry patterns

Subject: App stability cheat-sheet: SDK migration, endpoints, and retry patterns

Tim / Penta integrations team—

Per our kickoff, attached is a concise 'stability cheat-sheet' to make the SDK migration and endpoint cutover low-friction on your side. This thread will cover: SDK install & config, endpoint mapping for the new Redwood runtime, recommended retries/timeouts/backoff, rate-limit handling, and small sample snippets you can drop into your code.

High-level asks from Penta: confirm a 2-hour maintenance window on Dec 12, and identify one engineering contact who will be on the call for the cutover.

Key checklist (see attached sdk_migration_checklist.pdf for printable flow):
- Pre-cutover: verify API keys and environment variables (REDWOOD_API_KEY -> REDWOOD_MIGRATION_KEY), pin model versions for parity, and run smoke tests against staging.
- Cutover: switch client base URL (old: api.redwood.ai/v1 -> new: runtime.redwood.ai/v2) and use the compatibility header X-Redwood-Compat: legacy when doing a phased roll.
- Post-cutover: monitor token-per-request and 95th percentile latency for first hour; rollback policy: flip back to old routing via control-plane toggle if error rate > 3% for 10m.

Retry + timeout guidance (summary):
- Client-side timeout: per-request socket timeout 10s, overall request timeout 30s (adjust for long-gen calls).
- Retries: idempotent calls: up to 4 retries with exponential backoff (base 200ms), capped jitter, and final timeout guard. Non-idempotent generation calls: prefer client-side optimistic concurrency with idempotency tokens and only 1 retry on network failures.
- Rate-limits: default burst allowance: 60 RPS per API key; implement 429 handling with full-jitter backoff and yellow-card alerting when 429s exceed 1% of requests over 5m.

Attached: sdk_migration_checklist.pdf (one-page runbook), sdk_samples.zip (Node/Python snippets + Postman collection), rate_limit_matrix.csv (per-endpoint limits).

Next steps:
1) Confirm the maintenance window and POC on your side.
2) We’ll set up a Zoom for the cutover and provide a live tail of logs.

Thanks—
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
